newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER CAUTIOUS ABOUT 1997 TITLE CHANCES.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER CAUTIOUS ABOUT 1997 TITLE CHANCES.

text.p: Double world drivers' champion Michael Schumacher is sceptical about Ferrari's title hopes this year but believes 1998 could bring championship honours.
When the Italian team unveiled their new car at their Fiorano test track on Tuesday, Schumacher was cautious about Ferrari's prospects for the Formula One season starting in eight weeks.

Schumacher said: "My real hope is that we can compete for the championship and put pressure on the Williams team or any other that sets the pace, or that we will be under pressure from them, but I cannot predict that we will be champions.
"To be honest, I think this year we are looking for reliability and a big improvement on last year, but the real championship for us should come in 1998."
The German driver, who recently signed a new three-year contract which keeps him with Ferrari until 1999, said he had been impressed on his first close look at the new Ferrari F310B.

He supported British chief designer John Barnard's view it was more important to meet the post-Christmas deadline for the car's launch with a reliable competitor than to experiment with any risky innovations.

On a day when the launch took place inside a massive marquee at the snow-covered Fiorano circuit close to the team's historic headquarters, Barnard said meeting the deadline with a reliable car had been his priority.

However, Barnard added he had many revisions and modifications in the pipeline, some of which may be introduced after the eight weeks of initial testing, starting on Wednesday, which end before the season-opening Australian Grand Prix in Melbourne on March 9.
The new car, an evolution of Barnard's unreliable and troublesome, but adventurous, vehicle for 1996, showed several changes.
Barnard said the most notable were a fully-raised nose and modified side-pods which were designed to improve stability, aerodynamics and the high-speed handling of the car.
He said he planned to add modifications to the suspension, and later possibly the gearbox and other items, but could not reveal more.
Ferrari president Luca di Montezemelo was in buoyant mood at the launch but would not be drawn into predictions. "It is going to be a big battle this year," he said.

"Three years ago we were two seconds off the pace. Two years ago we had one win and last year we had three wins. In 1997 we want to win more races than last year and in 1998 we want to win the world championship."

For the first time, Ferrari are the only leading team being supported by Marlboro as sponsors and their car will carry one white chevron, a sign their budget -- already believed to be the biggest in the sport -- has been substantially enlarged by the cigarette manufacturers' coffers.
Schumacher's team mate, Briton Eddie Irvine, who endured a succession of 10 non-finishes last season, said he expected much greater reliability and more testing opportunities.
"I don't want another year like the last -- and that car was the most difficult I have ever had to work with," he said.
